subject: Dunhill Development Corporation Ltd. (original parent)
claim: Public Accounts 1974/75 records an agreement dated 25 January 1974 under which the Province acquired Dunhill shares through Woodbridge Development Corporation.
caveat: Contemporary financial-statement evidence of the agreement date; the executed agreement itself has not been recovered.

subject: Dunhill Development Corporation Ltd. (original parent)
claim: By 22 May 1974, the Province through Woodbridge had acquired sufficient Dunhill shares for Crown tax exemption. The next Public Accounts describes 22 May as the date it became a provincial Crown corporation.
caveat: This is not the date of incorporation or proof of direct 100% provincial share ownership on that day.

subject: Dunhill Development Corporation Ltd. (original parent)
claim: After Woodbridge was wound up, Dunhill became wholly owned directly by the Province on 7 June 1974.
caveat: The financial note does not give a separate exact date for Woodbridge winding-up; do not assign June 7 as its legal dissolution date.

subject: Dunhill Development Corporation Ltd. (original parent)
claim: The financial statements for the year ended 31 October 1974 identify eight wholly owned Dunhill subsidiaries: W.K.P. Construction Ltd.; Crown Lumber Limited; Fisher Developments Ltd.; Dunhill Homes Ltd.; Dunhill Holdings Ltd.; United Provincial Investments Ltd.; Ventures Realty Ltd.; Georgia Park Holdings Ltd.
caveat: Ownership observation in the consolidated statements, not the incorporation dates or first ownership dates of those subsidiaries. W.K.P. must not be silently equated with the original parent.

subject: Pemco Holdings Ltd. / Provincial Rental Housing Corporation
claim: The Housing Fund investment schedule reports all three issued Pemco common shares, cost $633,511, at both 31 March 1975 and 31 March 1976.
caveat: This establishes shareholding checkpoints, not the exact 1973 purchase date or a ministry accountability interval.

subject: Pemco Holdings Ltd. / Provincial Rental Housing Corporation
claim: A special resolution on 12 April 1976 changed the company name to British Columbia Housing Corporation, with the Registrar certificate dated 7 May 1976.
caveat: 12 April is the resolution date; the separately proved registry effective/certificate date remains 7 May 1976.

subject: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd.
claim: The first-year financial statements state that the company was incorporated under the Canada Corporations Act on 5 May 1975 to operate Princess Marguerite.
locator: F84, note 1(a); financial statements audited F80
caveat: Original financial-statement evidence; the federal certificate of incorporation itself was not obtained.

subject: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd.
claim: The company acquired British Columbia Steamship Company Inc., a separate Washington corporation, on 15 May 1975.
caveat: Keep the federal Canadian company and Washington company as distinct legal entities.

subject: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd.
claim: The company states that its share capital is held by five directors in right of the Province; the balance sheet lists five issued common shares.
caveat: A provincial beneficial-ownership observation, not evidence that the directors personally owned the company or proof of the responsible ministry.

subject: Urban Transit Authority of British Columbia
claim: Section 2 of the Urban Transit Authority Act became operative on 20 July 1978 under OIC 1931/1978, establishing the corporation.
locator: Act s2 and s25; OIC operative paragraph
caveat: Assent was 29 June 1978; the order was approved 13 July. The order commenced specified sections, not every provision.

subject: Urban Transit Authority Act
claim: OIC 1930/1978 charges the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing with administration of the Urban Transit Authority Act.
caveat: The assignment order precedes the corporation’s 20 July statutory establishment; do not start the body on 13 July.
object: Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing

subject: Urban Transit Authority of British Columbia
claim: The original Act requires at least eight directors, appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council from persons holding elected municipal office.

subject: Metro Transit Operating Company
claim: The Metro Transit Operating Company Act, including its establishing section 2, came into force on 18 January 1980 under OIC 29/1980.
caveat: Act assent was 31 July 1979 and order approval 10 January 1980. Commencement does not establish the date that each Hydro employee or asset was transferred.

subject: Metro Transit Operating Company
claim: Section 4 of the original MTOC Act provides for at least seven directors appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

subject: Urban Transit Authority of British Columbia
claim: The 1982 amendment changes the authority’s corporate name to British Columbia Transit, operative 12 August 1982.
locator: 1982 Act s3; OIC; 1991 s2 historical note
caveat: This is continuation/rename of the authority, not incorporation of a different corporation.

subject: British Columbia Transit
claim: The same 1982 amendment adds the express Crown-agent provision to the authority’s establishing section.
caveat: This claim concerns the express statutory agency clause, not a claim that no other Crown relationship existed before this date.

subject: British Columbia Transit Act
claim: OIC 1535/1982 transfers administration from the Minister of Municipal Affairs to the Minister of Education and transfers unspent Vote 66 money for Urban Transit Authority and Custom Bus Services.

subject: British Columbia Transit Act
claim: OIC 850/1983 repeals B.C. Reg. 366/82 and charges the Minister of Human Resources with administration of the British Columbia Transit Act.

subject: Metro Transit Operating Company
claim: The 1985 amendment’s new BC Transit Act section 2.1 transfers all MTOC property and rights to BC Transit and makes BC Transit liable for MTOC debts and obligations. The provision commenced on 1 June 1985.
caveat: A transfer/assumption event. The provision does not itself declare MTOC dissolved.

subject: Metro Transit Operating Company
claim: OIC 1094/1985 selects every MTOC employee for transfer; the reproduced Public Accounts describes the employee and asset merger as effective 1 June 1985.
locator: 1985 Act s6; OIC 1094; Public Accounts note 18(e), printed B21
caveat: OIC 1094 says the effective date of this order rather than spelling out June 1. June 1 is explicitly reported in Public Accounts and matches commencement of the enabling section. Do not use its May 30 approval stamp as the employee-transfer date.

subject: Metro Transit Operating Company
claim: OIC 1096/1985 appoints nine MTOC directors and its chair effective 1 June 1985, while OIC 1095 appoints the BC Transit board.
caveat: This is affirmative evidence against automatically treating the 1985 asset transfer as MTOC legal dissolution. Its ultimate legal end remains unproved.

subject: Metro Transit Operating Company Act
claim: The 1991 official consolidation prints that the Act is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources.
caveat: An observation in this edition, not the assignment order or proof that Human Resources administered the Act from its 1980 start.

subject: Liquor Distribution Branch
claim: The branch-establishing section 2 of the Liquor Distribution Act became operative on 31 December 1976 under OIC 3494/1976.
locator: Act ss2,28; OIC; 1991 s2 historical note
caveat: Assent on 26 June 1975 and administrative historical references to 1975 are different milestones. Order excludes ss16(3),17(1), but includes s2.

subject: Liquor Control and Licensing Branch
claim: The branch-establishing section 2 of the Liquor Control and Licensing Act became operative on 31 December 1976 under OIC 3490/1976.
caveat: The order excepts ss31,35,38(1),61,63(2)(b),(c); it is not commencement of all provisions.

subject: Government Liquor Act and Liquor-control Plebiscites Act
claim: OIC 3493/1976 repeals both predecessor Acts effective 31 December 1976.
caveat: Repeal of legislation is not by itself a separately worded corporate dissolution order for the old Liquor Control Board.

subject: Liquor Distribution Act
claim: OIC 3495/1976 charges the Minister of Consumer and Corporate Affairs with administration of the Liquor Distribution Act.
caveat: Assignment order was made before the 31 December commencement of the branch-establishing provision.
object: Minister of Consumer and Corporate Affairs

subject: Liquor Control and Licensing Act
claim: OIC 3491/1976 charges the Minister of Consumer and Corporate Affairs with administration of the Liquor Control and Licensing Act.
caveat: Assignment order was made before the 31 December commencement of the branch-establishing provision.
object: Minister of Consumer and Corporate Affairs

subject: Liquor Distribution Branch and Liquor Control and Licensing Branch
claim: In Hansard the responsible minister states that the two branches’ budgets were split on 1 April 1977.
locator: Question 97, Hon. K.R. Mair response, pp 5210–5211
caveat: A budget separation, distinct from 1975 assent and December 1976 statutory commencement.

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim: The Power Development Act 1961 vested BC Electric shares in the Crown and deemed the Act effective from 2 p.m. Pacific Standard Time, expressly excluding daylight saving time, on 1 August 1961.
caveat: This 1961 enactment was subsequently held ultra vires according to the contemporary Hydro report; the 1964 acquisition statute separately gives retroactive authority. Do not present the 1961 text as the whole legal story.
local_time: 14:00 PST, expressly not daylight saving time

subject: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (1962 enactment)
claim: The 1962 Act purports to amalgamate BC Electric and the BC Power Commission as BC Hydro. OIC 839 brings the Act into force on 30 March 1962.
locator: Act s3 and OIC operative paragraph
caveat: Retain this historical commencement, but qualify its subsequent judicial invalidation and the 1964/1965 legal reconstruction.

subject: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (1962 enactment)
claim: OIC 840/1962 appoints the initial directors and appoints Gordon M. Shrum and Hugh L. Keenleyside co-chairmen.
caveat: Appointments under the original 1962 scheme; distinguish the later 1964 statutory authority.

subject: Power Development Acts and original Hydro Act
claim: Hydro’s contemporary annual report states that Chief Justice Lett held the 1961 Power Development Act, its 1962 amendment and the 1962 Hydro Act ultra vires on 29 July 1963.
caveat: The annual report is contemporary primary corporate evidence of the judgment; the full reported judgment has not been recovered in this package.

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim: Hydro reports a settlement agreement dated 27 September 1963 with BC Power Corporation following the share valuation, and the Power Measures Act 1964 expressly ratifies that agreement.
locator: Report p17 and note 1 p22; 1964 Act s4
caveat: Keep the settlement date separate from the original 1961 takeover date and later 1965 amalgamation.

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim: The BC Electric Company Limited Acquisition Act 1964 authorizes acquisition of all common shares as at 1 August 1961 for $197,114,358 and provides retroactive effect.
caveat: Enactment date is 20 March 1964; its operative acquisition date is deemed back to 1 August 1961. Preserve both fields.

subject: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (1964 statutory corporation)
claim: The new 1964 Hydro Act establishes the statutory corporation. OIC 773 orders its proclamation, and OIC 2519 expressly records that the proclamation brought the Act into force on 23 March 1964.
caveat: A new legal constitution under the 1964 Act; the operational historical lineage still reaches 1962.

subject: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (1964 statutory corporation)
claim: The 1964 Act makes the authority an agent of the Crown and makes the Minister of Finance its fiscal agent.
caveat: Fiscal-agent status is not proof that Finance held every aspect of ministerial responsibility for Hydro.

relationships.object: Crown in right of British Columbia

subject: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority (1964 statutory corporation)
claim: The 1964 Act gives appointment of the authority’s directors to the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited and British Columbia Power Commission
claim: OIC 2386/1965 approves their amalgamation with the 1964 Hydro authority, with effectiveness to be set in the parties’ agreement.
caveat: This is the authorizing instrument; the agreement provides the exact effective time.

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited and British Columbia Power Commission
claim: The agreement reproduced in the Power Measures Act 1966 takes effect at 5 p.m. local Vancouver time on 20 August 1965. The three bodies continue as the Hydro authority established under the 1964 Act, and BC Electric and the Power Commission cease separate corporate existence.
locator: 1966 Act s3 and Schedule clauses 1–2, printed pp241–242
caveat: The ratifying Act assented on 1 April 1966 expressly validates the 20 August 1965 agreement. Do not date the amalgamation to the later assent.
successor: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority established by the 1964 Act

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim: OIC 2387/1965 separately revokes and cancels BC Electric’s incorporation and declares it dissolved after reciting that the amalgamation had already occurred.
caveat: This is the later formal corporate cancellation/dissolution event; the agreement says separate existence ceased on 20 August.

subject: British Columbia Electric Company Limited
claim: Power Measures Act 1966 section 5 deems the Crown-held BC Electric common shares surrendered to Hydro and cancelled immediately upon the amalgamation.
caveat: Statutory retroactive confirmation, assented to 1 April 1966.

subject: Vancouver Wharves (1993 acquisition subject)
claim: On 30 March 1993 the Minister of Transportation and Highways publicly acknowledged BC Rail’s recently completed Vancouver Wharves purchase.
locator: Oral Questions, BC Rail Purchase of Vancouver Wharves Ltd.
caveat: A latest-confirmed date for the purchase, not the exact closing date or executed acquisition agreement.

subject: Vancouver Wharves (1993 acquisition subject)
claim: A July 1993 reprint expressly credited to BC Rail Coupler says Vancouver Wharves would remain a separate company with its own board and management after acquisition; 98 of its 111 acres were already leased from BC Rail.
caveat: Corporate announcement reproduced in a railway publication; useful contemporary governance evidence, but not a registry identity match or legal transfer instrument.

subject: Vancouver Wharves (1993 acquisition subject)
claim: A 1997 secondary railway history gives 25 March 1993 as the purchase date.
caveat: Do not import as an exact closed date. No contemporary primary closing record has yet corroborated the day.

subject: Vancouver Wharves Limited Partnership
claim: Ministerial Order 5/2004, signed 30 December 2003, approves the BC Rail reorganization transactions; Schedule A(j) describes transfer of BC Rail Ltd.’s 75% interest in Vancouver Wharves Limited Partnership to BCRC or an affiliate.
locator: Railway Certificate 6497; Schedule A(j); Schedule B
caveat: Approval and planned transaction terms, not proof of closing. This is a limited-partnership interest, not 75% of an identically named company’s shares. The 2004 order number does not change the 2003 signature date.
object: British Columbia Railway Company or affiliate

subject: British Columbia Harbours Board
claim: Sections 2 and 3 of the Harbour Board Repeal Act commenced under OIC 1061/1985 on 30 May 1985, repealing the Harbour Board Act, dissolving the board and terminating members’ appointments. The date is expressly confirmed in Public Accounts.
locator: 1983 Act ss2,3,8; OIC 1061; Public Accounts 1984/85 C24 note 19(b)
caveat: The repeal Act assented on 23 September 1983; that is not the board’s dissolution date. Sections 4–5 authorize transfers to BC Development Corporation and BC Railway Company, but their precise transfer orders/dates are not supplied by OIC 1061.
